---
description: "Use when writing or editing PowerShell functions. Covers function help and parameter documentation."
applyTo: "**/*.ps1, **/*.psm1"
---
# PowerShell Function Documentation

- Document every function with comment-based help.
- For PlatyPS-generated help, make the first `.LINK` in every public function's help the hosted command page URL (`https://<project-owner>.github.io/<project>/docs/<ExportedCommandName>.html`). Derive the project URL from repository/module metadata and use the actual exported command name, including any manifest `DefaultCommandPrefix`. PlatyPS uses this first link for the generated `online version` metadata; put Microsoft or other reference links in subsequent `.LINK` entries.
- Document each parameter only at its declaration in the `param` block, using a concise comment immediately above that parameter. Do not repeat parameter descriptions in `.PARAMETER` comment-based-help sections or elsewhere in source.
- Write useful `.SYNOPSIS` and `.DESCRIPTION` sections and at least one runnable `.EXAMPLE` where appropriate. In every `.EXAMPLE`, include any setup or context commands a reader needs to reproduce the example, use the module's exported command name (including any manifest `DefaultCommandPrefix`), and put the primary command on its own line with its explanation on the following line. Include cleanup for resources the example creates when practical, and state external prerequisites such as Docker, network access, or a running service. Show the expected output after the explanation. When practical, run the exact example end-to-end and use captured output rather than inventing values. Replace or redact personal information such as account names, machine-specific paths, and temporary identifiers; identify any redactions. If an example cannot be run, label its output as illustrative rather than captured. For variable or environment-dependent values, indicate which values may vary; when a command has no output, state that explicitly.
- Before editing generated Markdown, inspect the repository's help-generation task and use its narrow documentation-update task (such as `Doc.Update`) rather than a broader build that may clean docs. Review the rendered pages for accurate syntax, parameter descriptions, examples, and valid related links. If PlatyPS does not surface parameter-definition comments, do not duplicate them in `.PARAMETER` help to work around it; investigate a compatible generation approach and report the limitation if none exists.
- Generate or refresh Markdown help with the repository's existing documentation task (prefer its narrow Invoke-Build target) in place. Do not generate help in a temporary directory. Do not hand-copy parameter descriptions into generated pages when that would create a second source of truth.
- Inspect documentation-task output for non-terminating errors even if the task reports success. Compare affected pages with current source help after generation: update tools can retain stale prose. If needed, use a supported command-specific help-generation option in place, preserving unrelated pages and existing edits; report any unresolved errors or generator limitations.
- Search affected generated pages for unresolved `{{ Fill` or `{{ Add` placeholders before finishing. Do not overwrite or reformat unrelated generated pages.
- Avoid `.LINK` entries unless the generated Markdown links have been verified as valid.
- After any change to a public function, update the changelog to document the modification.
